sections.history: Tiruchattimutram, also spelt Tirusakthimuttram, is an ancient Shaiva village near Patteeswaram, some seven to eight kilometres from Kumbakonam on the banks of a Kaveri branch. Hymned in the Tevaram by Appar and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams, the shrine was first built in brick and later rebuilt in granite under Raja Raja Chola I; inscriptions of Raja Raja I, Kulothunga III and the Vijayanagara kings survive on its walls, marking a span of patronage across centuries.
sections.architecture: The temple follows the Dravidian plan with a gopuram, prakara and the sanctum of Sivakozhundeeswarar; the goddess Periyanayaki has her own shrine. The lingam is revered as the one the goddess embraced in her penance, a motif the temple shares with the great shrine at Kanchipuram. The granite fabric of the Raja Raja period and its inscriptions make the temple a quiet record of Chola building beside the Kaveri.
sections.legends: The defining tradition is Parvati's penance. By one account the goddess, to demonstrate that loving devotion is the sure path to grace, did severe tapas here — standing on one foot and embracing the lingam, as she did at Kanchipuram. Pleased, Shiva granted her his grace. From this the lord takes the tender name Sivakozhundeeswarar, the green sprout of Shiva, and the temple is believed to bless devotees who pray here for marriage and a worthy partner.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Shaiva festival calendar — Maha Shivaratri, Pradosham, the Margazhi season and the annual Brahmotsavam. The goddess's penance legend gives particular meaning to the festivals of Parvati, and the shrine draws those praying for marriage, especially on the goddess's days.
sections.experience: Tiruchattimutram offers the pilgrim a temple where the goddess herself is the model devotee — she who stood on one foot and embraced the lord. The darshan of Sivakozhundeeswarar, the tender sprout of Shiva, and the shrine's association with marriage give the quiet delta temple a gentle, hopeful draw, close to the great centres around Kumbakonam.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruchattimutram is near Patteeswaram in Thanjavur district, about 7-8 km from Kumbakonam; Kumbakonam is the nearest rail head, with local buses and taxis to the village.
